title: Design exercise: SAA-4.3-S04
scenario: Brightwater Hydrology Board keeps everything in one oversized relational database whose cost keeps rising. It holds three workloads: readings from 6,000 river gauges, each reporting every 15 seconds and never edited afterwards, read almost only as rolling averages over recent hours or days for groups of gauges; nine years of survey records, about 3 billion rows of 60 columns, scanned by five analysts who use 4 columns per query a few times a week; and a permit registry of 900,000 rows where clerks update individual rows inside transactions spanning three tables. Dashboards read the gauge data constantly, while the analysts' scans currently slow the registry down.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
The platform team will not operate self-managed database servers
The total monthly database run-rate must not exceed today's single relational database
Procurement rejects any service that is closed to new customers

rubric.label: Each of the three workloads is placed on a database type chosen from its own read and write pattern in the scenario, and none is left on a type built for another pattern just because it already exists
Analyst scans no longer compete with the permit registry's transactions, and for each workload the record names the scenario figure that drives its saving and what would be measured to confirm it

constraint_reason: Mapped as design_exercise to complete skill coverage when no dedicated live lab step exists
